youtubeTitle: The Gospel and Soul Health Session 6 - Dr Bruce Wauchope
chapter: 6th Non-negotiable: Through His loving Union and Solidarity with us as the 2nd Adam, whatever happened to Jesus as a human being happened to us and the entire human race
topic: Union: whatever happened to Jesus happened to us
summary: Bruce sets out the sixth non-negotiable: because Christ makes and sustains all things and has entered both what the Trinity made and what we made (darkness), whatever happened to him as a human happened to us and to the whole human race. Our 'creation' of darkness is not a making but an omission: a blindness to the love that is still there. Jesus entered a split humanity and worked through its darkness to meet himself, the Father and the Spirit within, and he shares that healing with us as a being, not as a technique. When darkness met the incarnate God, it killed him, so our deicide was our suicide; God undid our violence non-violently, like a judo throw. Without union, the New Testament verses about dying, rising and being born again with Christ make no sense. With union, they are the foundation of inner healing: Christ is in us, and the accuser's message of separation is a lie.
keyPoints: Humans do not create in the way God does. Darkness is our 'creation' by omission: we choose not to participate with love, a possibility opened by the freedom we were given.

Jesus entered a body held together by himself, worked through the split and darkness in that humanity, and met himself, the Father and the Spirit within. He shares that capacity for coming home with us.
The gospel is not a christological technique for climbing back. It is a being, Jesus, who has done it and shares it from within us.
We are not autonomous 'battery packs'. 'Without me you can do nothing' and 'what do you have that you did not receive?' show that our life is not our own.
Because he is in union with us and sustains us, what happens to Christ in his incarnation happens to us. That is the core of the gospel.
At his baptism Jesus said, 'it is fitting for us to fulfil all righteousness'. He was setting our righteousness right, not his own.
When the Word came to a darkened world, he exposed our false knowledge of God and we killed him. Because of union, our deicide was our suicide.
The Trinity submitted to our violence and so undid it non-violently, like the armies in 2 Chronicles 20 destroying each other, or a judo throw.
Jesus refused Satan's offers of power, spectacle and institutional control. No kingdom of God is built with the methods of darkness.
Athanasius: 'We saw our life hanging on the cross.' The rulers, human and angelic, crucified the Lord of glory because darkness knows life but not love (1 Corinthians 2:7-8).

Without union these verses are nonsense: 'one died for all, therefore all died'; 'crucified with Christ'; 'born again through the resurrection'; 'made alive together with Christ'. Baptism is our agreement with what has already happened to us.

T.F. Torrance: the secret of every person, whether they believe it or not, is bound up with Jesus. So the accuser's message, 'you're no good, you're separated', is a lie. Jesus came to fix us, not merely to forgive us.

keyTerms.definition: Christ as the new head of humanity: what happens to him happens to the whole race.
Christ's loving identification with every human being through union.
Darkness is not something we make but a failure to participate with love: blindness to what is.
By killing the one who sustains us, humanity took itself down into death with him.
God undoing our violence by submitting to it rather than overpowering it.
What Christ accomplished for every person without their permission, before they believed.
The internal voice that says 'you're no good' and, with our pain, convinces us we are separated.

quotes: My deicide of Jesus is my suicide.
If you do not see the union, you cannot see the gospel.
I was born again 2,000 years ago when the only beloved Son of God rose from the dead. (T.F. Torrance)
It's not about getting forgiveness. It's about getting fixed up.

caseStudy.title: The relentless 'woodpecker'
caseStudy.scenario: Grace, 31, was baptised as a teenager but now feels she has 'lost' her salvation after a period of depression and a broken relationship. A voice in her head repeats that she's no good and that God has left. She keeps rededicating her life at church services, hoping to feel connected again. Each time the feeling fades, she feels more separated.
caseStudy.analysis: Grace's accuser and her deep pain work together to convince her she is separated, which Bruce calls a lie produced by dualistic thinking. In the gospel of union, she died and rose with Christ 2,000 years ago, and her baptism was her agreement with that. Her secret is bound up with Jesus whether she feels it or not. Her task is not to climb back but to participate in what is already true.
pathway: Learn to name the 'woodpecker' voice as an accuser, not as truth about her standing with God.
Read Galatians 2:20 and 2 Corinthians 5:14 daily as statements of fact rather than goals.
Revisit her baptism as an agreement with what Christ already did, not a contract she has broken.
Share her experience with a safe friend or small group instead of carrying it alone.
Seek professional support for depression alongside pastoral care, since both matter.

practices.name: With-Christ statements
practices.how: Each morning, say aloud: 'I died with Christ, I was raised with Christ, Christ is in me and I never put him there.'

practices.name: Read Athanasius together
practices.how: As Bruce recommends, read 'On the Incarnation' aloud with friends a chapter at a time, and discuss what stands out.

practices.name: Answering the accuser
practices.how: When an inner voice says 'you're separated', write down its claim, and beside it write the union verse that answers it.

reflection: How does 'whatever happened to him happened to us' change how you see your own salvation?
Where are you still treating the gospel as a technique you have to perform?
What does 'our deicide is our suicide' reveal about human violence and God's non-violence?

options: Whatever happened to Jesus as a human happened to us and all humanity
Humans must climb back to God
Only believers are united with Christ
quiz.explain: Through union and solidarity as the second Adam, his story is ours.

quiz.q: According to T.F. Torrance, when was he born again?
options: 2,000 years ago, when Christ rose from the dead
When he was baptised as a child
quiz.explain: Torrance located our new birth in Christ's resurrection (1 Peter 1:3).

quiz.q: What does Bruce say baptism is?
options: The way we climb back to God
Our agreement with what has already happened to us in Christ
quiz.explain: In baptism we agree that we died and rose with Jesus.
